Nicholas II reigned from 1894 until his abdication in March 1917, which was during the February Revolution (note: the Russian calendar was 13 days behind, so February in Russia was March in the Gregorian calendar). After his abdication, the Provisional Government took over, but later the Bolsheviks seized power in the October Revolution. The Romanov family was executed in 1918.

So the monarchy ended with Nicholas's abdication.

Also, the user might not know about the abdication details, so the answer should state he was forced to abdicate in 1917, which led to the end of the monarchy.

So the answer in Finnish would be Nikolai II, and maybe add a bit of context: that he abdicated in 1917 during the revolution, and was later executed.

Venäjän viimeinen tsaari ennen vuoden 1917 vallankumousta oli **Nikolai II Romanov**. Hän hallitsi Venäjää vuodesta 1894 vuoteen 1917, kunnes joutui luopumaan valtaistimesta helmikuussa 1917 (marraskuussa 1917 uudessa järjestelmässä) tapahtuneen Kansallisen vallankumouksen (ns. helmikuun vallankumouksen) seurauksena. Tämä johti Venäjän keisarikunnan päättymiseen ja Romanov-suvun valtakauden loppumiseen. Nikolai II sekä hänen perheensä teloitettiin myöhemmin heinäkuussa 1918.
